question:
A 89-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes reports that she has had
progressive difficulty walking during the past year and has fallen twice. Her legs often feel heavy after
she has been walking, causing her to limit her activities. When she sits down, her symptoms resolve
completely within a few minutes. She noticed the symptoms most recently while at the grocery store
but reports that she can typically finish shopping if she walks bent over the cart. She notes that walking
uphill is easier than walking downhill. The patient has no bowel or bladder symptoms. She has had
diabetes-related numbness in her feet for several years, but she reports that her blood sugar has been
under relatively good control and that her current symptoms are different from those associated with
her previous neuropathy. On examination, her mental status and cranial nerves are intact. She has
normal strength in all four extremities, with normal bulk, tone, and reflexes. She has no sensory level
but exhibits diminished sensation to light touch and pinprick in a stocking-glove distribution, with
decreased vibration sense and proprioception at both great toes. Which one of the following tests is
most likely to confirm the diagnosis in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) MRI of the lumbar spine (B)

MRI of the brain (C) Nerve conduction studies (D) Spinal tap (lumbar puncture) (E) Serum vitamin B12
testing (F) X-ray of the lumbar spine (G) Ankle-brachial index (H) Doppler ultrasound of the lower
extremities (I) Electromyography (J) Nerve-conduction study of the lower extremities
 A. Nerve conduction studies
B. MRI of the brain
C. Electromyography
D. Spinal tap (lumbar puncture)
E. Nerve-conduction study of the lower extremities
F. Ankle-brachial index
G. MRI of the lumbar spine
H. Doppler ultrasound of the lower extremities
I. Serum vitamin B12 testing
J. X-ray of the lumbar spine
